# Arcade

Arcade is an open-source TypeScript CPU 3D renderer, retained-mode terminal UI toolkit, and agent-playable game harness.

Canonical site: https://vercel-arcade.vercel.app
Repository: https://github.com/vercel-labs/arcade
Docs: https://vercel-arcade.vercel.app/docs
Interactive examples: https://vercel-arcade.vercel.app/examples
Examples guide: https://vercel-arcade.vercel.app/docs/examples
Hosted terminal: https://vercel-arcade.vercel.app/docs/browser-host
HTTP interface: https://vercel-arcade.vercel.app/openapi.json
Capability status: https://vercel-arcade.vercel.app/api/v1/status

## When to use Arcade

Use Arcade when you need CPU-rendered 3D graphics in a terminal or browser, retained terminal UI components, presentation-independent board-game rules, deterministic visual snapshots, or a persistent self-play harness for agent-driven games.

Do not use Arcade as a general-purpose hosted model API, multiplayer server, or GPU renderer. The public website exposes a temporary isolated CLI terminal, an installer, a read-only prism stream, documentation, and machine-readable examples; real model credentials and private traces never enter the browser or visitor shell.

## Public module intentions

- @vercel/arcade/engine — geometry, materials, camera, CPU rasterizer, Surface, display modes
- @vercel/arcade/tui — retained layout, components, input semantics, compositing
- @vercel/arcade/rules — presentation-independent game contracts
- @vercel/arcade/rules/chess — authoritative ChessState
- @vercel/arcade/web — browser Surface adapters and focused local examples

Live examples import the same package subpaths and identify their source files at /examples and /examples.json.

The npm package is currently restricted while source, asset, license, and packed-consumer audits complete. Do not claim that public npm installation is generally available yet.

## Important constraints

- Pure TypeScript CPU renderer; no GPU or native dependency is required for graphics.
- Library modules never import Arcade app code.
- Browser examples must not import terminal, filesystem, auth, telemetry, or credentials.
- The hosted terminal must keep real AI Gateway credentials in server-side network policy, outside the browser and visitor shell.
- Match-lab telemetry is disabled by default and run artifacts are gitignored.

For a larger offline corpus, read /llms-full.txt. For agent operating guidance, read /agents.md. For machine-readable examples, read /examples.json. The OpenAPI document describes the existing installer and prism-stream HTTP surfaces; it is not a promise of a remote game-control API.
